evidence: Receiving DO2 11.41 mg/L at 50.0 h then 1.90 mg/L at 50.2 h, persisting 1.60-1.96 mg/L through 52.0 h — below 2.0 mg/L minimum
No analogous collapse in source-1/2/3, which stay ~8-14 mg/L through 96 h
P assay 3.06 g/L at 48 h (delayed 4 h) — production active pre-collapse
Forward model: transfer multiplier 0.423, cost 3.46 estimated from change at ~50 h
Model comparison: strong_feed_reduction best (min DO 1.04, deficit 5.55, below-limit 9.2 h, mass 194.5 kg) vs combined (0.91/7.61/9.6/194.0) and increase_air (0.82/9.64/13/193.9)
args.rationale: At 50.2 h the receiving batch's DO2 abruptly fell from ~11.4 to ~1.9 mg/L and remains below the 2.0 mg/L operating floor through the decision time (52.0 h), unlike any source batch. The source-calibrated forward model attributes this to a severe drop in oxygen-transfer capacity (~42% of nominal), so the highest-magnitude bounded intervention is warranted. Among allowed actions, strong_feed_reduction (feed x0.6, air x1.15) minimizes predicted time below the oxygen limit and oxygen deficit while retaining essentially full product mass (predicted ~194.5 kg, the highest of all interventions, since growth continues under restored-but-partial oxygen supply). A stop would count zero production; KEEP or air-only would prolong oxygen-limit violation. The model flags even this action as marginally infeasible under nominal parameters, so this is the best available bounded choice pending review; an extra product assay was not requested because product concentration is not the binding issue — oxygen constraint compliance is, and waiting (KEEP) during assay turnaround would extend the violation.
args.uncertainty: The forward model is nominal, source-calibrated, and not the hidden receiving realization; all sensitivity members show minimum DO below 2.0 mg/L, so the intervention may not fully restore constraint compliance — a follow-up aeration repair/review beyond the bounded action set may be needed. P assays lag 4 h, so the true current product state is uncertain; product mass could differ. Sensor noise (~±0.3 mg/L) is small relative to the collapse magnitude, so the anomaly itself is high-confidence.
